about: The priest bows low, lays his joined hands on the altar and asks that an angel carry the offering to the altar on high. The angel is not named, and the tradition has never settled who he is: some saw Michael, some Christ Himself, some the Holy Spirit — a reading the old commentators rejected — and some refused to name him at all. Sublíme altáre — the altar on high — echoes Revelation 8. The petition rides on rogámus with the imperative iube; the ut clause has one verb (repleámur), with a generalizing clause about those who will communicate wedged in front of it.

s01.narrative: The priest bows low and lays his joined hands upon the altar.

s02.translation: In humble prayer we ask You, almighty God: command that these gifts be borne by the hands of Your holy Angel to Your altar on high, in the sight of Your divine majesty:

s04.translation: so that all of us, who

s11.translation: through this participation at the altar receive the most holy Body and Blood of Your Son

s05.narrative: The priest joins his hands and signs the cross once over the Host and once over the chalice.

s08.translation: may be filled with every grace and heavenly blessing.

s10.translation: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: An adjective — we, the suppliant — rendered adverbially here: it describes the posture the rubric has just commanded.

w007.function: An accusative neuter plural: the subject of the infinitive “perférri” (w008).

w008.function: The passive infinitive of a compound of fero, which is irregular and belongs to no conjugation.

w012.function: Singular: one angel, unnamed. The tradition has never settled who he is.

w023.function: The comma after ut sets off the whole clause about those who communicate, which is wedged between the conjunction and its verb “repleámur” (w041).

w024.function: The subject of “sumpsérimus” (w035) — hence nominative, though the form marks no case; the whole relative clause has wedged itself between “ut” (w023) and its verb.

w028.function: An ablative with “ex” (w025): not mere presence but the receiving of a share — see the lemma.

w029.function: The epithet of what the priest is about to name: the most holy — inviolable — Body and Blood; the lemma tells the word’s Roman story.

w035.function: A future perfect: the receiving is to be complete before the petition for grace is fulfilled. The form can also be a perfect subjunctive, and a clause sitting inside a purpose clause can be drawn into that mood with it; the sense of the generalizing clause — as many as SHALL HAVE received — is what tips this edition to the future perfect.

w040.function: An ablative with “repleámur” (w041): that with which one is filled.
